title: R2 — Mixed Autonomous Sand
lede: Sand is the threat you see first. The real team is a network of independent clocks that can keep winning after Sand stops mattering.
philosophy: R2 is built around a simple idea: never make one piece of infrastructure responsible for the whole team. Sand can create overwhelming speed for Excadrill, but Salamence, Rillaboom, Gholdengo, and Milotic can form a complete second team without it. The pilot's job is not to force Sand every game. It is to identify which resource the opponent has the hardest time stopping, create that resource cheaply, and hand the resulting turn to the teammate that converts it best.
meta: Regulation M-C Pokémon Champions doubles. This manual treats Coil / Hypnosis / Muddy Water / Protect Milotic as the default R2 control-scaler. Nature, item, and Champions SP recommendations below are starting points for this architecture, not claimed tournament-optimized damage or speed benchmarks.

pilot.thesis: Do not ask, 'How do I make Sand work?' Ask, 'Which of my clocks becomes easiest to activate when they respect Sand?'
pilot.beginnerTranslation: R2 looks like a Sand team, but you should think of it as several smaller teams sharing the same six Pokémon. Sometimes Tyranitar and Excadrill are the stars. Sometimes they are distractions that make Gholdengo or Milotic easier to set up. A good R2 player changes plans before the opponent's answer becomes useful.

coreArchitecture.identity: A modular balance team with an explosive Sand branch and a fully functional non-Sand branch. Its strongest turns come from converting small resources such as Fake Out, Intimidate, Tailwind, weather control, or forced targeting into either immediate damage or a setup turn.
coreArchitecture.primaryEngine: Tyranitar creates Sand and Excadrill converts it into immediate speed and pressure.
coreArchitecture.conversionModel: Infrastructure is deliberately shared. Sand feeds Excadrill; Fake Out and Intimidate manufacture setup turns; Tailwind feeds every offensive member; forced defensive responses to physical pressure give Gholdengo and Milotic room to scale.
coreArchitecture.scalingModel: Gholdengo scales offensively through Nasty Plot. Milotic scales defensively and operationally through Coil, then converts accuracy into reliable Hypnosis and Muddy Water. These two scalers attack very different forms of counterplay.
coreArchitecture.controlModel: Rillaboom controls tempo with Fake Out and terrain. Salamence controls physical damage with Intimidate and speed with Tailwind. Tyranitar controls weather. Milotic controls individual threats through sleep and Muddy Water accuracy pressure.
coreArchitecture.speedModel: The team can win through Sand Rush, Tailwind, priority Grassy Glide, or by refusing the speed race and letting Milotic scale. R2 therefore does not have one speed mode.
coreArchitecture.resourceModel: The six repeatedly creates free or reduced-cost turns. Fake Out, Intimidate, weather replacement, Ground immunity, Grassy Terrain, Protect pressure, and offensive double-target threats all create turns that another node converts.
threatProfile: Dual-Mega preview pressure from Tyranitar and Salamence
Distributed Dragon answers through Draco Meteor, Rock pressure, Steel pressure, and sleep
Rain disruption through Sand plus Rillaboom

architecture.summary: Tyranitar, Salamence, and Rillaboom manufacture the team's most important resources: Sand, speed control, Intimidate turns, Fake Out turns, terrain, and forced targeting.
Excadrill converts Sand into immediate KOs; Gholdengo converts protected turns into Nasty Plot or Make It Rain pressure; Milotic converts passive or physical boards into Coil and Hypnosis control.
The match usually finishes through one of four clocks: Sand Rush cleanup, boosted Gholdengo spread damage, stabilized Milotic control, or Rillaboom priority after the opposing board has been chipped.

clocks.goal: Turn Sand into a short damage race the opponent cannot stabilize before Excadrill takes a decisive KO.
Use Tailwind to turn otherwise fair attackers into consecutive first-move threats.
Find one low-cost Nasty Plot turn, then force the opponent to survive repeated special spread pressure.
Reach a board where Milotic is too physically durable to remove comfortably and accurate enough to make Hypnosis and Muddy Water oppressive.
Turn accumulated chip into Grassy Glide cleanup while Fake Out and terrain keep the opposing offense from regaining tempo.

winRoutes.name: Sand Collapse
requires: Tyranitar can establish or re-establish Sand
Excadrill is positioned safely enough to attack
sequence: Use Excadrill's Sand Rush to move before conventional speed control can stabilize.
Threaten two-target pressure with Rock Slide plus Tyranitar's damage or a focused double target.
Use the resulting numerical or positional advantage to finish with Excadrill, Tyranitar, or a back-line cleaner.
winRoutes.finish: Excadrill remains faster than the surviving board and the opponent no longer has enough healthy pieces to trade efficiently.
winRoutes.failurePoint: Sand is removed, Excadrill is heavily Intimidated, or the opponent presents a board that safely absorbs Ground / Steel / Rock pressure.

winRoutes.name: Tailwind Conversion
requires: Salamence gets a safe Tailwind turn
At least one high-value converter remains healthy
sequence: Use Salamence's Intimidate or immediate Draco / Hyper Voice pressure to make an attack into Salamence inefficient.
Set Tailwind when the opponent spends the turn defending, switching, or reducing damage.
Bring in Gholdengo, Excadrill, or Rillaboom under the speed advantage.
Use the remaining Tailwind turns for high-value attacks rather than unnecessary setup.
Finish with priority, spread damage, or Sand after Tailwind expires.
winRoutes.finish: The opponent enters its final two Pokémon already chipped or down a piece while R2 still has a priority or weather endgame.
winRoutes.failurePoint: Salamence is removed before Tailwind or the opponent's speed mode ignores Tailwind entirely.

winRoutes.name: Golden Free Turn
requires: A Fake Out, Intimidate, Protect, forced switch, or passive opposing turn creates setup access
Gholdengo is not under immediate overwhelming Ground, Dark, or Fire pressure
sequence: Use Rillaboom or Salamence to reduce the opponent's productive actions.
Place Gholdengo beside the connector rather than exposing it alone.
Take Nasty Plot only when the opponent is paying more to stop the partner than it can spend punishing Gholdengo.
Convert the boost immediately through Make It Rain or the appropriate single-target attack.
Preserve Gholdengo if one more protected turn can create a second spread-damage cycle.
winRoutes.finish: A boosted Gholdengo controls both opposing slots and forces defensive turns that the back line converts.
winRoutes.failurePoint: The pilot becomes greedy and uses Nasty Plot when immediate damage was already enough.

winRoutes.name: Coil Lock
requires: Milotic can survive the next physical exchange
The opponent cannot immediately remove or invalidate Milotic
sequence: Use Intimidate, Fake Out, terrain recovery, or offensive pressure to reduce the cost of Milotic's first Coil.
Coil raises Defense while improving the accuracy of both Hypnosis and Muddy Water.
Put the most dangerous opposing converter to sleep instead of trying to win its stat race directly.
Use Muddy Water to keep making progress while the partner pressures the second slot.
Protect when necessary to preserve Competitive boosts, sleep turns, or terrain recovery.
winRoutes.finish: Milotic becomes a durable control piece that repeatedly removes one enemy action while its partner wins the remaining one-on-one exchange.
winRoutes.failurePoint: Strong special pressure, status immunity, or immediate Taunt-style denial prevents the first Coil or makes Hypnosis unavailable.

winRoutes.name: Weather Inversion
requires: The opponent depends materially on Rain or another weather state
sequence: Hold Tyranitar until replacing weather changes more than damage.
Switch Tyranitar in to remove the opposing weather.
Use the same switch to activate Sand Rush Excadrill.
Force the opponent to spend another action restoring its weather.
Convert that forced weather action with Rillaboom pressure, Excadrill damage, or Milotic setup.
winRoutes.finish: The opposing weather setter becomes a tax instead of an engine and R2 controls the tempo of subsequent weather changes.
winRoutes.failurePoint: Tyranitar is exposed too early and removed before the decisive weather exchange.

failureRoutes.why: The opponent denies Sand, walls Excadrill, or repeatedly Intimidates the physical mode.
failureRoutes.fallback: Stop spending turns restoring Sand unless it creates immediate value. Transition into Salamence / Rillaboom support for Gholdengo or Milotic.
failureRoutes.nextRoute: Golden Free Turn or Coil Lock

failureRoutes.why: Gholdengo is pressured too aggressively to set up.
failureRoutes.fallback: Use the pressure aimed at Gholdengo as a reason to attack immediately, pivot, or let Milotic become the scaler instead.

failureRoutes.why: Milotic faces strong special pressure, status immunity, or setup denial.
failureRoutes.fallback: Do not force Coil. Treat Milotic as a bulky Muddy Water / Protect piece and move the clock to Gholdengo, Sand, or Tailwind.

failureRoutes.why: The opponent uses Trick Room or another speed state that makes moving first undesirable.
failureRoutes.fallback: Stop racing speed. Preserve Salamence for Intimidate and use Milotic or bulkier Tyranitar positions to play a slower resource game.

engines.label: Sand Rush Overdrive
path: Tyranitar · enter and establish Sand
Excadrill · gain Sand Rush speed
Tyranitar · threaten Rock / Dark pressure
Excadrill · force immediate Ground / Steel / Rock damage
Opponent · Protect, switch, or lose material
Back line · convert the forced defensive turn
engines.how: This is the obvious engine, which is exactly why it is so useful even when you do not intend to win through it. Tyranitar turns one field effect into both a weather advantage and Excadrill speed. Excadrill then forces the opponent to respect immediate damage, which often produces Protects and switches. Those defensive actions are resources for the rest of R2: Salamence can Tailwind, Gholdengo can find Nasty Plot, or Milotic can find Coil. Press this engine hardest when the opponent has no comfortable Ground immunity or weather reset. Do not confuse 'Sand is available' with 'Sand must be the win condition.'
engines.dependsOn: Excadrill must be healthy enough to convert Sand immediately, and Tyranitar must not be sacrificed before weather matters.
engines.disrupt: Weather replacement, Intimidate, Ground immunities, priority, defensive Steel / Ground answers, or removing Tyranitar before Excadrill activates.
engines.fallback: Use the opponent's Sand answers as information. If they overcommit to physical denial, rotate into Gholdengo or Milotic.

engines.label: Manufactured Free Turn
path: Rillaboom · Fake Out or Salamence · Intimidate
Opponent · loses damage or one action
Gholdengo / Milotic · survive the reduced-pressure turn
Gholdengo · Nasty Plot or Milotic · Coil
Connector · attacks, pivots, or protects the scaler
Scaler · converts the boost on the next exchange
engines.how: R2's most important engine is not Sand; it is the creation of cheap setup turns. Rillaboom can remove one opposing action with Fake Out, while Salamence can make an entire physical board hit less hard with Intimidate. The scaler beside them spends that reduced pressure on Nasty Plot or Coil. This is why R2's pieces feel more connected than a normal balance team: the support action is not the end goal, it is a currency that another Pokémon spends. Use this engine when the opponent's board is threatening but not capable of overwhelming both slots at once. If the setup turn is not truly cheap, attack instead.
engines.dependsOn: The connector must meaningfully reduce the opponent's productive actions for one turn.
engines.disrupt: Ghost / immunity interactions into Fake Out, special attackers ignoring Intimidate, Taunt-style setup denial, or overwhelming double-target pressure.
engines.fallback: Use the connector's tempo for immediate damage instead of setup; the same Fake Out or Intimidate turn still has value.

engines.label: Tailwind Bridge
path: Salamence · enter for Intimidate or immediate Dragon pressure
Opponent · defends against Salamence or its partner
Salamence · Tailwind
Fast converter · enters or begins attacking
Partner · pressures the second defensive answer
Rillaboom / Sand · carries the game after Tailwind expires
engines.how: Tailwind is the bridge between R2's Sand and non-Sand identities. It lets Excadrill function even when Sand is inconvenient, turns Gholdengo into a much harder immediate damage threat, and lets Rillaboom use strong Grass attacks without relying only on priority. Salamence is especially good at creating Tailwind turns because Intimidate and Draco Meteor make ignoring it dangerous. Press Tailwind when two or more teammates gain meaningful action order from it; do not spend a turn on Tailwind merely because the move exists. The ideal Tailwind does not win the battle by itself. It delivers the board to a cleaner that remains useful after the four-turn clock ends.
engines.dependsOn: At least two members of the current four should gain meaningful conversion value from moving first.
engines.disrupt: Trick Room, extreme priority, opposing Tailwind mirrors, or removing Salamence before it can set speed.
engines.fallback: Use Salamence as an Intimidate / Draco Meteor bridge and move the win condition to Milotic or Sand.

engines.label: Coil Into Control
path: Connector · reduce incoming physical pressure
Milotic · Coil
Milotic · gain Defense and accuracy
Milotic · Hypnosis the highest-value converter
Partner · attack the remaining active slot
Milotic · Muddy Water while sleep / Protect cycles preserve control
engines.how: Coil Milotic is not here to be an Ice Beam coverage patch. Its job is to attack the idea of scaling itself. Coil makes physical removal harder while simultaneously making Hypnosis and Muddy Water more dependable. That means one move improves survival, disruption, and damage consistency at the same time. Use this route when the opponent wants several turns to turn one Pokémon into an unbeatable board state, especially physical boosters or bulky setup pieces. Milotic does not need to erase their boosts if it can deny the boosted Pokémon actions. The opponent's correct answer is often to pressure Milotic early, which creates space for R2's other clocks.
engines.dependsOn: Milotic must receive at least one turn where Coil does not cost more board position than it gains.
engines.disrupt: Strong special double targets, status immunity, setup denial, or immediate burst before the first Coil.
engines.fallback: Use Muddy Water and Protect as low-commitment control while Gholdengo, Salamence, or Sand becomes the actual clock.

engines.label: Turn Their Weather Off
path: Opponent · establish Rain or weather-dependent offense
Tyranitar · switch in and replace weather
Excadrill · gain Sand Rush
Rillaboom · threaten Water / Ground pieces
Opponent · spend an action restoring weather
R2 · attack or set up during that restoration
engines.how: Against Rain, Tyranitar does much more than reduce Water damage. Replacing Rain can remove Swift Swim speed, weaken Water attacks, and change how moves such as Electro Shot function, all while activating Excadrill. Rillaboom then pressures the Water / Ground structures that commonly accompany Rain. The important beginner lesson is to avoid treating Tyranitar as a Turn 1 obligation. Weather control is strongest when the switch itself destroys an opposing plan that is already committed to the field. If the opponent must repeatedly return to its weather setter, those switches become predictable actions that R2 can convert.
engines.dependsOn: Tyranitar must remain available for the weather exchange instead of being traded too early.
engines.disrupt: Repeated opposing weather resets, immediate Water pressure into Tyranitar, or removing Rillaboom before the Water / Ground core is controlled.
engines.fallback: Use Rillaboom as the primary Rain pressure and let Milotic / Gholdengo play the longer game while Tyranitar is preserved.

network.thesis: R2 wins by turning small board-state resources into different clocks, then switching clocks when the opponent overanswers one.

commandments: Sand is one engine, not the identity of every game.
A free setup turn is valuable only if the boost converts before the opponent resets the board.
Preserve Tyranitar against weather teams until changing weather changes the actual turn.
If the opponent overcommits to stopping the physical mode, stop proving that the physical mode works and hand the game to Gholdengo or Milotic.
Before selecting four, name your primary clock and your fallback clock.

megaPool.role: Primary Sand Mega when raw physical pressure, weather permanence, and Rock / Dark damage matter most.
Alternative Mega when Tailwind, Intimidate sequencing, special Dragon pressure, and a more autonomous non-Sand game matter more.

roster.title: Tyranitar
roster.role: Weather root, physical breaker, Rock pressure, and preview anchor.
roster.primaryJob: Create Sand at the moment Sand changes the board, then make the opponent pay for respecting Excadrill.

training.label: Adamant offensive Sand root
training.why: Recommended starting spread: maximize immediate physical conversion while keeping strong natural bulk. Exact speed benchmarks should be adjusted after matchup testing.
training.rule: 66 SP max, 32 per stat; recommended starting spread, not claimed damage-calced optimal.

moves.name: Rock Slide
moves.why: Spread Rock pressure that converts Sand turns and punishes Flying threats such as Salamence.

moves.name: Knock Off
moves.why: Strong Dark pressure that also attacks the opponent's resource economy by removing items.

moves.name: Low Kick
moves.why: Coverage for heavy Steel, Rock, and opposing Tyranitar-style targets that resist the primary STABs.

moves.name: Protect
moves.why: Preserves the weather setter and lets Excadrill or another partner exploit the opponent's focus.

roster.objective: Do not spend Tyranitar like a disposable attacker when its future Sand switch is worth more than its current damage.
roster.howToPlay: Against neutral teams, Tyranitar can begin the damage race. Against Rain or weather-dependent teams, often keep it back so its entrance deletes the opponent's infrastructure at the moment they need it most.
abilityStages: Mega timing adds raw combat power while preserving the team's Sand identity.
roster.itemLoop: Mega only when the extra Tyranitar stats matter more than preserving Salamence as the possible Mega choice.
opening: Does Sand immediately create a safe Excadrill attack?
Does the opponent have weather that makes Tyranitar more valuable in back?
Is Tyranitar the correct Mega this game?
Can Rock Slide pressure two important targets at once?
answers: Special attackers that struggle into Tyranitar's natural special bulk

roster.title: Excadrill
roster.role: Sand converter, Steel attacker, Ground breaker, and immediate tempo clock.
roster.primaryJob: Turn Tyranitar's weather into immediate action advantage before the opponent can stabilize.

training.label: Jolly max Attack / Speed
training.why: Recommended starting spread because Excadrill's architectural job is immediate conversion. Specific speed benchmarks should be tested rather than assumed.
training.rule: 66 SP max, 32 per stat; recommended starting spread.

moves.name: High Horsepower
moves.why: Primary single-target Ground conversion without relying on spread Ground damage that conflicts with partners.

moves.name: Iron Head
moves.why: Steel pressure for Ice- and Fairy-type targets and an important direct answer to Baxcalibur-style Dragons.

moves.name: Rock Slide
moves.why: Fast spread pressure under Sand that complements Tyranitar's targeting and punishes Flying targets.

moves.name: Protect
moves.why: Lets Sand turns, partner pressure, and opponent targeting create safer follow-up attacks.

roster.objective: Make every Sand turn expensive for the opponent.
roster.howToPlay: Excadrill should rarely spend its strongest speed turns making low-value attacks. Ask which target must disappear before Sand ends. If physical denial becomes excessive, Excadrill has already done part of its job by pulling answers away from Gholdengo and Milotic.
roster.itemLoop: Focus Sash supports one guaranteed conversion attempt when healthy; avoid wasting it on incidental chip when the matchup requires Excadrill to survive a decisive hit.

scales: Not primarily a scaler; its value spikes through external speed infrastructure

opening: Is Sand active or about to become active?
Which target must be removed before Sand expires?
Will the opponent answer with Intimidate, Ground immunity, or Protect?
If Excadrill attacks now, what does that create for the back line?

roster.title: Salamence
roster.role: Universal bridge: Intimidate, Tailwind, Dragon execution, Ground immunity, and alternate Mega.
roster.primaryJob: Change the terms of the battle without committing the six to one engine.

training.label: Modest special pressure / Speed
training.why: Recommended starting spread for the special Tailwind / Draco Meteor bridge role. Adjust bulk and speed only after identifying concrete tournament benchmarks.
training.rule: 66 SP max, 32 per stat; recommended starting spread.

moves.name: Hyper Voice
moves.why: Reliable spread special pressure that gives R2 a damage axis unaffected by Intimidate.

moves.name: Draco Meteor
moves.why: Critical immediate Dragon punishment that lets Milotic keep Coil / Hypnosis instead of carrying Ice coverage.

moves.name: Tailwind
moves.why: Creates a second speed engine so the team is not dependent on Sand Rush.

moves.name: Protect
moves.why: Preserves the bridge while the partner exploits Intimidate or the opponent overtargets Salamence.

roster.objective: Enter at moments where one Salamence action improves two or more teammates.
roster.howToPlay: Salamence is not just a damage dealer. Intimidate can buy Milotic a Coil, buy Gholdengo a Nasty Plot, or reduce the urgency of opposing physical setup. Tailwind gives the non-Sand half of the team a full speed engine. Draco Meteor prevents opposing Dragons from assuming Salamence is only support.
abilityStages: Pre-Mega Intimidate is an important resource and should often be captured before Mega evolution.
Mega evolution changes Salamence from connector into a stronger autonomous damage source.
roster.itemLoop: Do not Mega automatically. In games where Tyranitar is the more important Mega, Salamence can still perform its bridge job through Intimidate, Tailwind, and Draco Meteor.

converts: Physical boards weakened by Rillaboom terrain

opening: Does Intimidate materially reduce both opposing slots?
Is Draco Meteor needed to prevent a Dragon from setting up freely?
Will Tailwind benefit at least two members of the chosen four?
Is Salamence or Tyranitar the better Mega for this matchup?

roster.title: Rillaboom
roster.role: Tempo connector, Rain breaker, terrain controller, and priority cleaner.
roster.primaryJob: Create one-action advantages that another R2 piece converts immediately.

training.label: Adamant bulky offense
training.why: Recommended starting spread: maximize Grass damage while giving Rillaboom enough general bulk to survive repeated connector duty. Exact defensive thresholds are unverified.
training.rule: 66 SP max, 32 per stat; recommended starting spread.

moves.name: Fake Out
moves.why: Creates the cleanest one-turn resource on the team for Nasty Plot, Coil, Tailwind, or focused damage.

moves.name: Grassy Glide
moves.why: Turns accumulated chip into priority cleanup and gives the team a speed-independent finishing tool.

moves.name: Wood Hammer
moves.why: Immediate high-power Grass pressure, especially valuable into Water / Ground structures.

moves.name: Protect
moves.why: Keeps the connector available for terrain, priority, and late-game cleanup rather than trading it unnecessarily.

roster.objective: Use Fake Out and terrain to manufacture the turn the actual win condition needs.
roster.howToPlay: New players often overvalue Fake Out as a generic safe move. On R2, ask what Fake Out is buying. If it buys Gholdengo a boost, Milotic a Coil, Salamence Tailwind, or a decisive double target, it is excellent. If it merely delays the game without improving the next board, attack instead.
roster.itemLoop: Miracle Seed keeps Rillaboom's offensive conversion meaningful without sacrificing Protect.

scales: Endgame value increases as targets enter Grassy Glide range

opening: What exactly does Fake Out buy this turn?
Does terrain weaken an important Earthquake or Ground plan?
Is Rillaboom my Rain answer and therefore too valuable to expose early?
Can I preserve it until Grassy Glide becomes a win condition?

roster.title: Gholdengo
roster.role: Autonomous special scaler and primary punishment for opponents who overprepare for R2's physical half.
roster.primaryJob: Convert one protected turn into a special damage clock that ignores Intimidate.

training.label: Modest max SpA / Speed
training.why: Recommended starting spread for immediate special conversion after Nasty Plot. Exact speed and bulk benchmarks should be refined through testing.
training.rule: 66 SP max, 32 per stat; recommended starting spread.

moves.name: Make It Rain
moves.why: Primary spread conversion after a free turn; attacks both slots and punishes boards built to stop physical Sand.

moves.name: Shadow Ball
moves.why: Single-target special damage when Make It Rain's stat drop or targeting is undesirable.

moves.name: Nasty Plot
moves.why: Turns one manufactured free turn into a self-contained win condition.

moves.name: Protect
moves.why: Punishes overtargeting and helps cycle Fake Out, Tailwind, terrain recovery, or partner pressure.

roster.objective: Become the reason the opponent regrets spending its resources on Tyranitar and Excadrill.
roster.howToPlay: Gholdengo does not need Nasty Plot every game. Sometimes its best contribution is immediate Make It Rain while the opponent is still arranging its Sand answers. Use Nasty Plot when Rillaboom, Salamence, Protect pressure, or a forced switch makes the setup turn genuinely low-cost.
roster.itemLoop: Leftovers supports repeated Protect and setup cycles in slower packages.

protects: Physical attackers by forcing special answers

opening: Do I need Nasty Plot, or does immediate Make It Rain already create enough value?
Which physical answer is the opponent bringing that Gholdengo punishes?
Can Rillaboom or Salamence create a genuinely free boost?
Do I need Gholdengo healthy for a late Steel matchup?

roster.title: Milotic
roster.role: Adaptive control scaler, Intimidate inverter, and universal answer to opponents that need repeated setup turns.
roster.primaryJob: Make scaling strategies spend turns without receiving reliable actions in return.

training.label: Bold physical control
training.why: Recommended starting spread for the Coil / Hypnosis job: survive physical setup pressure long enough for Coil to compound. This is a role-based starting point, not a verified tournament calc.
training.rule: 66 SP max, 32 per stat; recommended starting spread.

moves.name: Coil
moves.why: Raises Defense and accuracy at once, improving survival, Hypnosis reliability, and Muddy Water consistency.

moves.name: Hypnosis
moves.why: Stops a boosted threat by denying actions instead of trying to erase its stat changes.

moves.name: Muddy Water
moves.why: Provides spread progress while Coil improves its reliability and potential accuracy-pressure value.

moves.name: Protect
moves.why: Preserves Coil investment, Competitive boosts, sleep turns, and terrain recovery.

roster.objective: Turn a board that wants to scale into a board where one opposing slot rarely gets to act.
roster.howToPlay: Milotic is not the team's Ice Beam slot. Draco Meteor, Rock pressure, and Steel attacks handle Dragons elsewhere. Milotic's value is broader: Coil lets it survive physical escalation, Hypnosis attacks any threat that depends on taking repeated actions, and Competitive punishes stat-lowering counterplay aimed at R2's physical side.
roster.itemLoop: Leftovers plus Protect and terrain recovery reward preserving Coil investment instead of trading Milotic quickly.

protects: Physical attackers from repeated Intimidate through Competitive threat

opening: Can Milotic take one Coil without losing the board?
Which opposing Pokémon becomes unacceptable if it gets three consecutive actions?
Is Hypnosis more valuable than racing damage?
Would the opponent's Intimidate accidentally activate my best alternate clock?

construction.thesis: Pair one explosive weather engine with multiple autonomous clocks so the opponent cannot solve the six by solving Sand.
construction.method: Use Tyranitar / Excadrill to create immediate respect, Salamence / Rillaboom to create low-cost turns, and Gholdengo / Milotic to convert those turns along different offensive and control axes.
construction.winCondition: Identify the least-correlated clock at preview, use the other threats to manufacture its activation turn, and preserve one fallback clock for the endgame.

endgames.label: Sand Rush Cleanup
endgames.path: Opposing Ground checks and priority are chipped or removed; Tyranitar restores Sand.
endgames.how: Excadrill moves first and finishes the remaining board with the appropriate single-target or spread attack.

endgames.label: Golden Board
endgames.path: Gholdengo reaches a boost or favorable Tailwind turn while its major Ground / Dark answers are damaged.
endgames.how: Make It Rain or Shadow Ball forces consecutive defensive turns until the opponent cannot cover both slots.

endgames.label: Coil Lock
endgames.path: Milotic has one or more Coils and the opponent lacks immediate special burst or status immunity.
endgames.how: Hypnosis removes one enemy action stream while Muddy Water plus the partner steadily wins the other slot.

endgames.label: Grassy Glide Checkmate
endgames.path: The faster opposing pieces have been chipped into priority range.
endgames.how: Rillaboom no longer needs to win the speed war because Grassy Glide converts accumulated chip directly into KOs.

packs.label: Sand Overdrive
packs.when: Bring this when the opponent lacks comfortable Ground / Steel answers, depends on conventional speed control, or cannot repeatedly reset Sand without losing tempo.
packs.identity: The most direct version of R2: immediate Sand pressure backed by Salamence's speed bridge and Gholdengo's special punishment.

identityCard.winCondition: Use Sand for immediate pressure; if the opponent overdefends physically, convert the breathing room into Gholdengo.
identityCard.clock: Fastest R2 package. Sand first, Tailwind second, Gholdengo last.
identityCard.commitment: Medium-high. This four wants active tempo and does not contain Milotic or Fake Out for recovery.
identityCard.autonomy: High because Salamence / Gholdengo remains a coherent special route when Sand is denied.
identityCard.triggerBreadth: Sand, Tailwind, Intimidate turns, physical defensive overcommitment.

chooseWhen: The opposing four is vulnerable to fast Ground / Steel / Rock pressure.
The opponent's best Sand answer is physical defense rather than immediate special burst.
You want to threaten a very fast Game 1 while still retaining Gholdengo as a different clock.
avoidWhen: Multiple physical setup threats make Milotic essential.
The opponent's board can comfortably reverse speed with Trick Room.
pilotDecision.previewQuestion: If they stop Excadrill, does that answer also stop Gholdengo?
pilotDecision.primaryMistake: Continuing to force Sand after the opponent has already spent its roster slots solving Sand.

strategy.opponentPattern: Conventional balance, speed-reliant offense, or teams whose Sand answer is primarily physical.
strategy.purpose: Force immediate Sand respect and punish the defensive response with special conversion.
refuses: Long passive games where Fake Out or Milotic control would be more valuable
Repeatedly restoring Sand without gaining an action
strategy.winCondition: Create a two-clock dilemma between Excadrill speed and Gholdengo special scaling.
strategy.gamePlan: Break with Sand → bridge with Intimidate / Tailwind → finish with the converter the opponent failed to cover.
strategy.mantra: Make them answer Sand, then punish the answer.
turnChecklist: Does Sand produce an immediate KO threat?
Which physical answer are they revealing?
Can Salamence turn that answer into Tailwind?
Does Gholdengo need Nasty Plot or just damage?
Which clock survives after weather ends?
strategy.defaultLeadWhy: Against boards that cannot immediately invalidate Sand, this pair forces the opponent to reveal its defensive plan before R2 reveals its fallback.

fieldPlan.leadWhy: The lead makes the opponent answer speed, Ground pressure, Rock pressure, and weather immediately. That information tells you whether the back-line special route should become primary.

backJobs.job: Reset physical pressure with Intimidate, establish Tailwind if Sand stops controlling speed, and threaten Dragons with Draco Meteor.
Punish physical defensive overcommitment and convert any forced Protect / switch sequence into special pressure.

fieldPlan.turn1: If the opposing lead cannot safely absorb Excadrill plus Tyranitar pressure, attack immediately; do not use a setup turn just because the back line contains setup.
bringInTriggers: Opponent commits Intimidate or Ground immunity into Excadrill → bring Salamence or Gholdengo and change axes.
Sand is removed but the opponent is still speed-reliant → bring Salamence and use Tailwind as the replacement engine.
Opponent begins protecting around Sand turns → bring Gholdengo to convert passive turns.

roles.macro: Create and restore Sand.
roles.micro: Choose whether this turn is about damage or preserving the next weather reset.

roles.macro: Convert Sand into immediate material advantage.
roles.micro: Target the piece whose removal makes the back-line clock easiest.

roles.macro: Bridge Sand into the non-Sand speed and special game.
roles.micro: Use Intimidate / Tailwind only when they change the following turn.

roles.macro: Punish physical defensive commitments.
roles.micro: Distinguish a real Nasty Plot turn from a greedy one.

loops.title: Sand Forces the Answer
loops.body: When Tyranitar plus Excadrill threatens immediate damage, attack the piece that makes the opponent's defensive structure function. If they Protect or switch to preserve it, use that revealed response to decide whether Salamence or Gholdengo should enter next. The board you want is one where the opponent has spent a defensive action while you still have Sand pressure or a fresh special converter.
loops.trigger: Opponent cannot ignore Sand Rush pressure.
sequence: Opponent reveals Protect, switch, Intimidate, or immunity.
R2 pivots into the route that punishes that answer.
loops.payoff: Information plus tempo without locking the team into Sand.

loops.title: Replace Sand with Tailwind
loops.body: If Sand is removed or Excadrill's Sand turns become awkward, bring Salamence into a physical attack or a predicted defensive turn. Use Intimidate to lower the immediate cost of Tailwind, then let Excadrill or Gholdengo convert the new speed state. The board you want is a fast mixed-offense position that no longer cares which weather is active.
loops.trigger: Sand no longer controls speed cleanly.
loops.payoff: A second independent speed engine.

loops.title: Their Sand Answer Becomes Gold
loops.body: When the opponent commits Intimidate, bulky physical walls, or repeated Protects to surviving Excadrill, stop asking Excadrill to break that structure. Bring Gholdengo into the lower-pressure turn and either attack immediately or Nasty Plot if the setup is genuinely safe. The desired board is boosted or healthy Gholdengo facing resources that were chosen to stop physical Sand.
loops.trigger: Opponent overcommits to physical Sand defense.
loops.payoff: Failure inversion: stopping Plan A opens Plan B.

forks.when: Their lead cannot comfortably stop Sand.
forks.then: Attack immediately and force the first defensive answer.
Preserve Excadrill and transition quickly into Salamence / Gholdengo instead of proving the bad matchup.

victims.name: Speed-reliant balance
victims.why: Sand Rush and Tailwind create two distinct ways to control action order.
victims.play: Force them to reveal which speed mode they prepared for, then use the other.
victims.trap: Do not spend both Salamence and Tyranitar merely maintaining speed.

victims.name: Physical-defense-heavy anti-Sand teams
victims.why: Gholdengo attacks from a special axis that their Sand answers may not cover.
victims.play: Use Excadrill to draw the answer rather than trying to overpower it.
victims.trap: Do not lose Gholdengo before the physical answers are committed.

counters.name: Hard Trick Room with immediate pressure
counters.why: This four is biased toward controlling conventional speed and lacks Milotic's slower control route.
counters.play: Use immediate damage and avoid unnecessary Tailwind.
counters.trap: Setting Tailwind into a guaranteed Trick Room can make your own positioning worse.

counters.name: Rain requiring Rillaboom
counters.why: Without Rillaboom, Water / Ground rain cores can force Tyranitar to carry too much of the matchup.
counters.trap: Do not treat weather control alone as a complete Rain answer.

advantages.title: Two speed engines
advantages.body: Sand Rush and Tailwind fail to different forms of disruption.

advantages.title: Mixed conversion
advantages.body: Excadrill punishes special-defense investment; Gholdengo punishes physical-defense investment.

hazards.title: Sand tunnel vision
hazards.body: The package becomes much worse if you spend multiple turns recreating Sand while the opponent calmly develops a stronger board.

packs.label: Autonomous Balance
packs.when: Bring this when Sand is awkward, weather is contested, the opponent is prepared for Tyranitar / Excadrill, or you want the highest density of independent non-Sand win conditions.
packs.identity: The hidden second team inside R2: Intimidate + Fake Out manufacture turns for two autonomous special/control scalers.

identityCard.winCondition: Manufacture one low-cost setup turn, then make the opponent choose between stopping a special damage clock and a sleep/control clock.
identityCard.clock: Medium-speed adaptive game with two very different scaling destinations.
identityCard.commitment: Low. Every member functions independently and the package can change its intended win condition midgame.
identityCard.autonomy: Extremely high; this is the package that proves R2 is not actually dependent on Sand.
identityCard.triggerBreadth: Fake Out, Intimidate, Tailwind, Competitive, Coil, Nasty Plot, terrain recovery, priority.

chooseWhen: The opponent overprepares for Tyranitar / Excadrill.

The matchup rewards repeated positioning and setup access.
You expect physical Intimidate cycling that can activate Milotic.

Excadrill's Ground pressure is required to remove a specific Steel threat.

Chipped fast targets with Grassy Glide
refuses: Forcing weather into a bad weather matchup
Racing every board on raw speed
strategy.winCondition: Make one scaler demand an answer, then let the other scaler exploit the resources spent on that answer.

backJobs.job: Enter into physical pressure, reset Attack with Intimidate, and establish Tailwind when the board wants faster conversion.

bringInTriggers: Opponent commits physical attackers → bring Salamence for Intimidate.

Gholdengo forces Protects → use the passive turn to reposition a connector rather than automatically Nasty Plotting again.

roles.macro: Control physical damage and speed.
roles.micro: Choose the exact turn where Intimidate turns into Tailwind or Draco pressure.

roles.macro: Manufacture tempo and preserve priority.
roles.micro: Fake Out the action that matters, not simply the easiest legal target.

roles.macro: Create the fast special scaling clock.
roles.micro: Take one high-quality Nasty Plot rather than two greedy ones.

roles.macro: Create the slow control clock.
roles.micro: Coil before Hypnosis when the board allows it; attack immediately when it does not.

loops.title: Fake Out Into Gold
loops.body: When one opposing slot is the clear source of immediate pressure and can be flinched, Rillaboom uses Fake Out while Gholdengo decides between Nasty Plot and immediate damage. If the second opposing slot cannot meaningfully punish Gholdengo, take the boost. The desired board is a boosted Gholdengo with Rillaboom still alive to provide priority or another terrain cycle later.
loops.trigger: One flinch meaningfully reduces the opponent's productive actions.
sequence: Opponent is forced to respect boosted special pressure.
Back line enters behind that pressure.
loops.payoff: A one-turn resource becomes a full special win condition.

loops.title: Intimidate Into Coil
loops.body: When the opposing board is primarily physical, bring Salamence into the attack and reduce the damage before Milotic commits to Coil. Milotic then becomes harder to remove while Hypnosis becomes more dependable. The desired board is a physically weakened opponent facing a Milotic that gets more difficult to attack every turn.
loops.trigger: Physical offense gives Salamence a safe Intimidate entry.
sequence: Milotic begins sleep / Muddy Water control.
loops.payoff: The opponent's physical clock slows while Milotic's control clock accelerates.

loops.title: The Second Scaler
loops.body: When the opponent starts spending both targeting and defensive resources on Gholdengo, stop demanding that Gholdengo win alone. Protect or reposition Gholdengo and bring Milotic into the reduced-pressure board. The board you want is one where their anti-Gholdengo actions have created the first safe Coil.
loops.trigger: Opponent overtargets Gholdengo.
sequence: Milotic takes Coil or begins control.
loops.payoff: The answer to one scaler activates the other.

loops.title: Sleep Creates Priority Range
loops.body: When Milotic has stabilized a dangerous opposing Pokémon with Hypnosis, use the sleeping turns to attack the second slot instead of repeatedly targeting the sleeper. Rillaboom and Salamence accumulate chip while Milotic uses Muddy Water. The desired board is an opponent waking up into Grassy Glide or Gholdengo KO range rather than a reset neutral board.
loops.trigger: Hypnosis lands on the opponent's main converter.
sequence: Milotic puts main threat to sleep.
loops.payoff: Control turns become damage progress rather than merely delay.

forks.when: Fake Out creates a genuine Nasty Plot turn.
forks.then: Take the boost and begin the Gholdengo clock immediately.
Attack or Protect rather than forcing setup; use Salamence / Milotic as the second wave.

victims.why: Salamence reduces physical damage while Milotic can punish opposing Intimidate through Competitive.
victims.play: Let the opponent's stat control decide which scaler receives the easier game.
victims.trap: Do not leave Milotic out of the four if Competitive meaningfully changes their best line.

victims.name: Teams whose Sand answer consumes several roster slots
victims.play: Make their anti-Sand preparation functionally dead.
victims.trap: Do not bring Tyranitar / Excadrill simply because they are the nominal core.

counters.name: Immediate strong special burst
counters.why: Intimidate and Coil are less helpful if both opposing slots attack specially and deny setup access.
counters.play: Prioritize Tailwind and immediate damage over slow setup.
counters.trap: Do not assume every board offers a Coil or Nasty Plot turn.

counters.name: Status immunity plus setup denial
counters.why: This can reduce Milotic's most universal anti-scaling route.
counters.play: Shift the primary clock to Gholdengo and Salamence.
counters.trap: Do not spend multiple turns forcing Hypnosis into an immune or protected route.

advantages.title: No Sand dependency
advantages.body: All four remain coherent even if weather never favors R2.

advantages.title: Two independent scalers
advantages.body: Gholdengo wants special damage conversion; Milotic wants a slower control board. Their failure conditions differ.

hazards.title: Setup greed
hazards.body: The presence of two setup Pokémon does not mean both should boost. Usually one is the clock and the other is insurance.

loops.title: Hold Tyranitar
loops.body: When the opponent can establish Rain on Turn 1 but does not immediately force a knockout, keep Tyranitar in back. Let Rillaboom pressure the Water / Ground converter first, then bring Tyranitar when Rain is actively powering speed or damage. The desired board is Sand appearing after the opponent has already committed its Rain attacker to the field.
loops.trigger: Rain matters more on the second exchange than on Turn 1.
loops.payoff: Weather replacement removes value instead of merely changing the icon.

loops.title: The Weather Flip
loops.body: When Tyranitar replaces Rain with Sand and Excadrill is healthy, immediately ask whether Excadrill can take a decisive Ground, Steel, or Rock action. Do not spend the weather flip on low-value chip. The desired board is one where the opponent must choose between restoring Rain and surviving Excadrill's new speed.
loops.trigger: Tyranitar successfully replaces Rain.
sequence: Excadrill pressures the key Rain piece.
loops.payoff: One switch simultaneously denies their engine and starts yours.

loops.title: Do Not Race the Tower
loops.body: When an Archaludon-style target begins accumulating Stamina or special boosts, avoid repeatedly feeding it weak physical hits. Use Excadrill's meaningful Ground pressure when a knockout is available; otherwise let Milotic Coil and threaten Hypnosis. The desired board is a sleeping or heavily pressured scaler while Rillaboom attacks the partner that was protecting it.
loops.trigger: Rain's bulky scaler is gaining more from the exchange than R2.
sequence: Attack the partner while the scaler is controlled.
loops.payoff: R2 attacks actions and infrastructure instead of losing a stat race.

forks.when: Rillaboom threatens their main Rain converter.
Their Turn 1 Rain attack is immediately catastrophic.
forks.then: Consider exposing Tyranitar earlier because the weather denial itself is worth the risk.

counters.play: Lean harder on Milotic control and use Excadrill only on decisive Sand turns.
counters.trap: Do not repeatedly pivot Tyranitar into attacks merely to change weather.

advantages.body: R2 does not rely on weather control alone; it also pressures the Pokémon trying to exploit Rain.

hazards.title: Weather ego
hazards.body: The goal is not to have Sand on screen more turns than the opponent has Rain. The goal is to own the turns where weather changes the result.

identityCard.clock: Control first, then Excadrill or Rillaboom cleanup.

identityCard.triggerBreadth: Dragon Dance, Bulk Up, Swords Dance, physical offense, passive setup, Intimidate.

loops.title: Intimidate Plus Fake Out
loops.body: When the opponent leads a physical scaler beside support, Salamence enters for Intimidate while Rillaboom uses Fake Out on whichever slot enables the setup most efficiently. If the scaler still boosts, its immediate damage is reduced; if it attacks, one action has already been removed. The desired board is a slower physical threat that Milotic can safely enter against.
loops.trigger: Opponent's primary win condition is physical setup.
sequence: Opponent's first setup turn loses efficiency.
loops.payoff: Milotic receives a cheaper first Coil.

loops.title: Coil Before the Coin Flip
loops.body: When Milotic can survive the next physical exchange, use Coil before relying on Hypnosis. The Defense boost makes the following turn safer while the accuracy boost makes Hypnosis and Muddy Water more dependable. The desired board is not simply a sleeping target; it is a Milotic that can repeat the control loop if the first sleep ends.
loops.trigger: Milotic gets a low-cost first setup turn.
sequence: Milotic uses Hypnosis on main scaler.
loops.payoff: Repeatable control rather than one desperate sleep attempt.

loops.title: Ignore the Sleeping Threat
loops.body: When Hypnosis lands on the opponent's central scaler, stop pouring attacks into the sleeping slot unless the knockout is immediate. Bring Excadrill or preserve Rillaboom and remove the active partner first. The desired board is the sleeping scaler waking up alone into a two-versus-one or priority endgame.
loops.trigger: Key scaler is asleep.
sequence: Second slot falls before sleeper regains control.
loops.payoff: Sleep becomes board compression instead of temporary delay.

loops.title: Milotic Opens Make It Rain
loops.body: When Milotic's Coil / Hypnosis threat causes the opponent to concentrate special damage or Taunt-style denial into Milotic, use Rillaboom's Fake Out or Tyranitar pressure to make a Gholdengo entry safe. Gholdengo should usually attack immediately unless the board truly grants Nasty Plot. The desired board is a special attacker facing resources that were chosen to stop a bulky Water control piece.
loops.trigger: Opponent commits anti-Milotic resources.
loops.payoff: The two scalers alternate rather than competing for setup turns.

forks.then: Consider Milotic as the primary clock because Competitive may make the intended counterplay actively bad.
Preserve Tyranitar and transition to Gholdengo rather than forcing physical damage.

victims.name: Slow balance
victims.why: The package has enough time to let the opponent reveal which scaler it is equipped to stop.
victims.play: Use the first turns for information and resource advantage.
victims.trap: Do not race a team that is already volunteering to play slowly.

counters.name: High-tempo special offense
counters.why: This four lacks Salamence Tailwind and Excadrill Sand Rush, so immediate special burst can deny both scaling routes.
counters.trap: Do not mistake theoretical late-game superiority for guaranteed setup access.

advantages.title: Incompatible answers
advantages.body: The resources used to stop boosted Gholdengo are often different from those used to stop Coil / Hypnosis Milotic.

hazards.title: Too much setup, not enough conversion
hazards.body: A +2 Gholdengo and +2 Milotic are not automatically better than one boosted threat plus immediate pressure. Spend boosts.

matchupScripts.name: Rain
matchupScripts.script: Preserve Tyranitar for the important Rain turn, use Rillaboom to threaten Water / Ground converters, and make the opponent pay every time it restores weather.

matchupScripts.name: Dragon-heavy offense
matchupScripts.script: Use Salamence's Draco Meteor and Intimidate for direct Dragon interaction, then use Milotic to prevent repeated setup turns.

matchupScripts.name: Anti-Sand balance
matchupScripts.script: Leave Tyranitar and Excadrill on the bench if their answers do not also solve Salamence / Rillaboom / Gholdengo / Milotic.

matchupScripts.name: Slow defensive balance
matchupScripts.script: Hide the real win condition until the opponent reveals whether it is better equipped to stop Gholdengo or Milotic.

matchupScripts.name: Neutral offense
matchupScripts.script: Force immediate respect with Sand, then use Salamence and Gholdengo to punish the first defensive adaptation.

victims.name: Teams with one-dimensional speed control
victims.why: R2 can access Sand Rush, Tailwind, priority, or a Milotic route that does not need to win the speed race.

victims.name: Intimidate-heavy physical control
victims.why: Gholdengo ignores Attack drops, while Milotic can actively profit through Competitive.

victims.name: Teams whose anti-Sand plan consumes multiple slots
victims.why: The Salamence / Rillaboom / Gholdengo / Milotic package can function as an entirely separate team.

victims.name: Physical setup teams
victims.why: Intimidate, Fake Out, Draco pressure, Coil, and Hypnosis attack the setup sequence from several directions.

counters.name: Fast special offense with little dependence on Attack drops
counters.why: It can reduce the value of Salamence's Intimidate and deny Milotic's first Coil before R2's slower engines activate.

counters.name: Status-immune or sleep-resistant scaling
counters.why: This attacks one of Coil Milotic's most important universal control routes and forces R2 to win through damage instead.

counters.name: Multiple simultaneous special scalers
counters.why: R2's strongest reactive tools are particularly efficient into physical progress. Two independent special clocks can strain Fake Out and Hypnosis because each action controls only one target.

counters.name: Hard Trick Room with immediate conversion
counters.why: Sand Rush and Tailwind can become poor resources if moving first is no longer the desirable speed state.

advantages.title: Embedded second team
advantages.body: Salamence / Rillaboom / Gholdengo / Milotic is a coherent bring-four with no dependence on Sand. Weather denial therefore does not erase R2's strategic identity.

advantages.title: Physical and special clocks
advantages.body: Excadrill and Tyranitar demand physical answers; Gholdengo attacks from the special side; Milotic attacks through control rather than direct stat racing.

advantages.title: Failure inversion
advantages.body: Intimidate can activate Competitive, physical Sand answers can create Gholdengo turns, and aggressive Gholdengo targeting can create Milotic turns.

advantages.title: Distributed Dragon interaction
advantages.body: Salamence supplies Draco Meteor and Intimidate, Tyranitar supplies Rock pressure, Excadrill / Gholdengo supply Steel pressure, Rillaboom suppresses Ground-heavy Dragon structures, and Milotic controls setup.

advantages.title: Rain interaction is architectural
advantages.body: Tyranitar does not merely change weather; its switch can remove Rain speed and damage while activating Excadrill, while Rillaboom independently pressures common Water / Ground converters.

advantages.title: Setup access from several sources
advantages.body: Fake Out, Intimidate, forced Protects, weather resets, and opponent overtargeting can all become the low-cost turn that Gholdengo or Milotic needs.

loops.title: Sand Pulls, Gold Pushes
loops.trigger: Opponent commits physical resources to surviving Tyranitar / Excadrill.
sequence: Preserve or pivot the Sand piece.
Convert with immediate special damage or Nasty Plot.
loops.payoff: The opponent's correct Sand response creates a special win condition.

loops.title: Physical Pressure Feeds Milotic
loops.trigger: Opponent relies on physical attackers or Intimidate.
sequence: Rillaboom can remove one action with Fake Out.
Milotic uses Hypnosis to deny the main converter.
loops.payoff: The opponent's physical game progressively becomes less efficient while Milotic's control becomes more reliable.

loops.title: Their Weather Starts Ours
loops.trigger: Opponent commits to Rain-dependent speed or damage.
sequence: Rillaboom pressures the Water / Ground converter.
loops.payoff: One switch denies their infrastructure and activates R2's.

loops.title: Control Becomes Grassy Glide
loops.trigger: Milotic or Salamence has slowed the opponent's damage output.
sequence: Priority closes without needing another speed-control turn.
loops.payoff: Slow control turns are converted into a speed-independent endgame.

hazards.title: Calling it a Sand team
hazards.body: The fastest way to pilot R2 badly is to believe Tyranitar + Excadrill must appear in every four. Sand is one architecture root inside a larger strategy generator.

hazards.title: Setting up because you can
hazards.body: Nasty Plot and Coil are only valuable when the following turn converts the investment. A free turn with no safe conversion is not actually free.

hazards.title: Using Fake Out without a purchase
hazards.body: Fake Out should buy Tailwind, Coil, Nasty Plot, a knockout, or a critical positional transition. Delaying the game by one turn is not automatically progress.

hazards.title: Sacrificing Tyranitar in weather matchups
hazards.body: Against Rain, Tyranitar's future switch can be worth more than its current attack because the switch may simultaneously remove several opposing resources.

hazards.title: Treating Milotic like coverage glue
hazards.body: Coil / Hypnosis Milotic is valuable because it attacks scaling as a strategy. Do not judge it by whether it has a super-effective move for every Dragon.

hazards.title: Forgetting the fallback clock
hazards.body: Before Turn 1, identify what happens if your first plan is denied. If the answer is 'I try the same plan harder,' you probably selected the wrong four.

evidence.source: Team-building framework and Ringside doubles manual structure supplied by the user; R2 architecture and Coil / Hypnosis Milotic reflect the preceding team-building discussion.
evidence.caveat: Training spreads and several held-item choices are recommended architecture-first starting points, not claimed tournament-calced optimizations. Validate exact Champions damage, bulk, and speed benchmarks on-device before locking a tournament registration.
